newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS LEADERS BACK PARTY CHIEF AGAINST PREMIER

Senior Congress leaders have closed ranks behind party chief Sitaram Kesri following his questioning by federal authorities. The Congress leaders, including Sharad Pawar, felt the questioning was aimed at forcing the Congress into a political quagmire. They decided to train their guns on the United Front government's economic policies and also issue a warning to the government that any designs on the Congress would boomerang. Pawar's support to Kesri was considered a major shot in the arm because of his earlier vacillation on supporting his leadership.
The Times Of India
SAUDI ARABIA WILL DEPORT 46 MORE CHILDREN

Saudi Arabia would deport another batch of 46 Indian children. These children, 40 boys and six girls, were illegally staying in the oil-rich kingdom and begging on the streets in holy places there. The Indian mission in Saudi Arabia said these children, most of whom came from Murshidabad in West Bengal, were lodged at the deportation centre in Jeddah and would be deported to India within a week. This would be the second batch of Indian children to be deported by Saudi authorities for overstaying illegally in the kingdom and earning their livelihood by begging. Recently, 77 children, 76 of them females, had been deported by the Saudi authorities.
Business Standard
CABINET TO DECIDE ON TATA-SIA COAL POLICY ON FRIDAY

The Cabinet will meet on Friday to take up a host of crucial issues. These would include the proposed Tata-Singapore Airlines (Tata-SIA) joint venture, uplinking for foreign broadcasters from Indian soil and a liberalised coal policy permitting imports and foreign investment in mining. Sugar and petroleum prices, and the Prasar Bharati Amendment Bill were also on the agenda.
PENSION FUNDS MAY BE ROUTED TO CORE SECTOR

The government is considering a proposal to earmark as much as two-thirds of the corpus of pension fund and part of the provident fund for investment in financial institutions and infrastructure. The United Front government had indicated in its common minimum programme that it would look for measures to tap this investment corpus of long-term funds. Sources said the current government's thinking was to release a portion of the investment corpus of these funds to finance long-term projects in the infrastructure sector. It was felt that this would also help develop a long-term debt market in the country.
BANKS START PROPRIETARY TRADING IN FOREIGN EXCHANGE MARKET

State Bank of India (SBI) and Bank of Baroda commenced proprietary trading in the foreign exchange market. The move followed the Reserve Bank of India's order allowing banks to fix their own open position limits. Earlier open positions were capped at 150 million rupees or $5 million. Sources said SBI's entry into the market had created a scare among foreign banks as it could make the market move the way it wanted because of SBI's huge volume of business.
DAEWOO TO ACQUIRE PART OF DCM STAKE

Daewoo Corporation negotiated a deal with the Vivek Bharat Ram family and associates to raise its stake in DCM Daewoo Motors. The automobile major would raise its stake in the passenger car joint venture from 75 percent to 87 percent at a price of 24 rupees per share. Sources said the board of directors of the company would also be reconstituted and the company name changed after the rights issue as DCM would be left with a minimal shareholding in the company. Sources said the deal, under which Daewoo would pick up the unsubscribed portion of the present rights issue including a part of the DCM stake, was expected to take effect after the closure of the 6.89 billion rupee rights issue of
SECURITIES WATCHDOG RULES OUT REVIEW OF OPEN OFFER PROVISION

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) ruled out a review of the clause in the proposed takeover code stipulating mandatory open offers by managements trying to consolidate holdings, even if they held over 51 percent in a company. Sebi said the clause had been adequately balanced by the exclusion of the primary market, particularly preferential allotments, from the purview of the takeover regulations. The P.N. Bhagwati Committee report on takeover had recommended that any acquisition of shares, above the creeping acquisition limit of two percent per year, would attract a mandatory open offer even if the present holding of the management was 51 percent, but less than 75 percent
Financial Express
DUTY-FREE IMPORTS UNDER EXPORT PROMOTION GOODS SCHEME

The Finance Ministry opposed the lowering of the existing 200 million rupee threshold limit for duty free import of capital goods under the Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme (EPCG). The inter-ministerial panel on the new export-import policy expressed their reservation on further relaxation of the scheme. Sources said the panel had agreed to consider the reduction in the customs duty on capital goods under the EPCG scheme only after the presentation of the 1997/98 (April-March) budget proposals. The Commerce Ministry, however, had favoured the lowering of threshold limit to help small-scale exporters compete in the international market.
BIRLAS, AT&T SAY NO TO GUARANTEE FOR TELECOM JOINT VENTURE

The Birlas and AT&T refused to issue corporate guarantees to their telecommunication joint venture, Birla-AT&T Communications Ltd. Sources said neither the Birlas nor AT&T would issue corporate guarantees to Birla-AT&T as sought by Industrial Development Bank of India as a precondition to disburse funds to the project. Birla-AT&T, therefore, initiated talks with the State Bank of India to fund the project. Corporate banking sources said the joint venture company was also talking to a few foreign banks, including ANZ Grindlays Bank and Bank of America, for rupee funding to the project.
REFORMS TO SPEED UP - POWER SECRETARY

Power Secretary P. Abraham promised a sea change in the sector to facilitate greater power availability in the years ahead. Steps in this direction would include greater authority to the states to clear power projects, dilution of the role of the Central Electricity Authority and allowing private sector in transmission. Abraham said the role of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board would be minimised by putting more projects on the automatic clearance route. He said the Union government would soon have an ordinance passed regarding private sector entry in transmission projects.
Business Line
OIL INDIA TO TAKE 10 PCT STAKE IN NUMALIGARH PROJECT

Oil India Ltd (OIL) decided to take up a 10 percent stake in the Numaligarh refinery project in Assam state. The acquisition, representing an equity holding of about 830 million rupees, would be the exploration and production company's first downstream foray. Sources said the promoters of the 26 billion rupee Numaligarh Refineries Ltd -- Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (32 percent), IBP Company (19 percent) and the Assam government (10 percent) -- had offered a stake in the project to OIL in 1996 itself. Sources expected the three partners to divest their holdings on a pro-rata basis to give OIL 10 percent stake.
SIEMENS, ABB SEEK TO BUILD POWER PLANTS IN INDIA

Swiss electrical giant Asea Brown Boveri and Siemens AG of Germany decided to approach the government for permission to set up two steam-based power plants in the country. The power plants would be set up within a time span of 48 months on a turnkey basis. On being permitted, the multinationals would take the independent power producers' route and look for a partner to set up the project. The president of the Federation of German Industries, Hans-Olaf Henkel, said a positive response to the two power projects and other such proposals would send the right message to potential German investors.
The Economic Times
TATA INFORMATION SYSTEMS TO SPLIT INTO TWO FIRMS

Tata Information Systems Ltd (TISL), the Tata-IBM joint venture in India, is to be vertically split into two companies. The services division of the company which looks after software, systems integration and other such services, is to be hived off into a separate company. TISL would, however, retain its name and function of selling IBM's mainframe and other computer hardware. Answering a question about TISL's services division becoming a separate company, Tata Sons Ltd chairman Ratan Tata said the Tatas would have a stake in the new company. He, however, declined to comment on the equity base and the investment ratio for the Tatas and IBM in the new company.
The Observer
TELECOM WATCHDOG MAY EVEN BE NON-STATUTORY BODY

The government may initiate moves to set up the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) as a non-statutory body if there is delay in getting the bill passed in Parliament. Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is said to have suggested that the Telecom Commission chairman keep its option open to set up TRAI as a non-statutory authority. The Finance Ministry's suggestion is significant considering that the previous government had also managed to have a similar bill on TRAI cleared by the cabinet, and failed to place it before Parliament. The bill was then withheld from being tabled as it was feared that the bill would not have secured majority support in both Houses of Parliament.
MANUFACTURING, SERVICES PLAY KEY ROLE

The impressive performance of both the manufacturing and the services sectors helped push up the overall gross domestic product (GDP) growth rate to 7.1 percent during 1995/96 (April-March). This was against 7.2 percent GDP growth rate in the previous year. In absolute terms, India's GDP at constant prices amounted to 2,742.09 billion rupees in 1995/96, as against 2,560.95 billion rupees in 1994/95. The 7.1 percent growth in GDP was largely due to manufacturing, electricity, trade, hotels and restaurants, railways, transport and communication sectors, even as agricultural output registered a negative growth of 0.3 percent during this period.
